baseline: Current v2 adapter; full BANC v888; C_STRICT; exp_lif_mps; MuJoCo position actuators
question: Does eliminating population-size dilution and/or releasing adhesion when a neural joint target lifts a pad improve forward movement?

hypotheses.name: unit_response
hypotheses.change: Replace mean linear population response with an additive, bounded per-neuron rate response: equivalent Hz = sum(100*r/(100+r)). Equal unit capacity is an engineering hypothesis, not measured slow/fast force calibration.

hypotheses.name: lift_release
hypotheses.change: Veto neural pad adhesion when the current neural target would lift its tip by >0.02 mm along the floor normal, estimated using the current physical joint Jacobian. No imposed phase, clock, route or root force.

hypotheses.name: combined
hypotheses.change: Both registered changes, with individual ablations above.

fixed.world: default_world with sources and obstacles empty
inputs: DNg100 20mV continuously on the two annotated DNg100 IDs

selection: A candidate must pass the unchanged walking gate in both inputs to qualify for live/default adoption. Report partial movement changes separately without promoting a failed walk.
followup: Only a qualifying candidate gets baseline/candidate comparisons at yaw ±0.15 rad, friction 0.7 and 1.3 (four predeclared pairs per input), plus sensor-off and motor-disconnect causal controls. No default change if screening fails.
stop: Stop each case on physics/neural fault. If all three candidates fail walking, preserve all raw evidence, leave v2 as default, and do not run the larger matrix or add more candidates in this experiment.
excluded_claims: autonomous gait from evoked DNg100 response
